exercises.title: Welcome
hints: Replace todo() with a number.
The check at the bottom says which number.

exercises.title: Type errors are the first teacher
hints: The annotation says string. Look at the value on the right.
Make the value a string that matches the check below.

exercises.title: Asking for hints
hints: Two plus three. Replace todo() with an expression that evaluates to 5.

exercises.title: A program is a value
hints: Effect.succeed takes the value the program should finish with.
Effect.runSync(program) runs the program and returns its result.

exercises.title: Nothing runs until you run it
hints: Effect.sync takes a function. Put the counter update inside it.
Effect.sync(() => { calls += 1 })

exercises.title: The Effect type
hints: The first type argument is what the program finishes with.
"hello" is a string, 3 is a number, and a Date is a Date.

exercises.title: Running with a Promise
hints: runPromise returns a Promise, so await it.
await Effect.runPromise(program)

exercises.title: Succeed is eager, sync is lazy
hints: Effect.succeed(x) receives x already computed, so the increment happens while building.
Wrap the increment in a function and give it to Effect.sync.

exercises.title: Failing
hints: The value you pass to Effect.fail is the error. The check tells you which string.
Effect.fail("out of stock")

exercises.title: Exit: success or failure as a value
hints: runPromiseExit never rejects. Await it to get an Exit value.
Exit.isSuccess(exit) and Exit.isFailure(exit) answer yes or no.

exercises.title: Wrapping a Promise that cannot reject
hints: Effect.promise takes a function that returns a promise, not the promise itself.
Effect.promise(() => loadGreeting())

exercises.title: Wrapping a Promise that can reject
hints: Effect.tryPromise takes an object with two functions: try and catch.
The catch parameter is typed unknown, so error.message does not compile yet. Narrow it first with instanceof Error.
catch: (error) => (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error))

exercises.title: Wrapping code that can throw
hints: Same shape as tryPromise: an object with try and catch.
Effect.try({ try: () => JSON.parse(input), catch: () => "invalid json" })

exercises.title: Deciding at run time with suspend
hints: suspend takes a function that returns an Effect. Put the if inside that function.
Effect.suspend(() => mode === "on" ? Effect.succeed("on") : Effect.fail("off"))

exercises.title: A program that returns nothing
hints: It is a value, not a function. No parentheses.
const done = Effect.void

exercises.title: Wrapping a callback
hints: The function you give to Effect.callback receives a resume function.
Call resume(Effect.succeed(value)) when the callback fires.

exercises.title: Waiting
hints: Durations can be written as text, like "20 millis" or "1 second".
Effect.sleep("20 millis")

exercises.title: Translate: plain functions
hints: Which one can throw? That one needs try, the other needs sync.
sync for double, try for mustBePositive.
catch: (error) => (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)), the same narrowing as in the tryPromise exercise.

exercises.title: Translate: promise-returning functions
hints: fetchScore never rejects. fetchRank can.
promise for the first, tryPromise for the second.
catch: (error) => (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)), the same narrowing as in the tryPromise exercise.

exercises.title: Translate: node-style callbacks
hints: The callback receives (error, value). Its error is typed Error | null, so error.message is fine here.
resume(Effect.fail(error.message)) for the error, resume(Effect.succeed(value)) otherwise.

exercises.title: Capstone: pick the constructor
hints: For each one ask: is it a plain value, does it run code, can that code throw, is it a promise, can it reject?
Constructors in play: succeed, fail, void, sync, try, promise, tryPromise.

exercises.title: Transforming a result with map
hints: .pipe(...) takes functions that transform the thing on its left.
price.pipe(Effect.map((n) => n * 1.5))

exercises.title: Two spellings of the same call
hints: The effect itself moves to the first argument.
Effect.map(price, (n) => n * 2)

exercises.title: The pipe function
hints: pipe(start, f, g) means g(f(start)).
pipe(3, double, addOne) and pipe(Effect.succeed(3), Effect.map(double), Effect.map(addOne))

exercises.title: Chaining maps
hints: One .pipe call can take many steps, separated by commas.
.pipe(Effect.map((s) => s.trim()), Effect.map((s) => s.toUpperCase()), Effect.map((s) => s + "!"))

exercises.title: Chaining programs with flatMap
hints: The function you give to flatMap returns an Effect, not a plain value.
userId.pipe(Effect.flatMap(loadUser), Effect.map((user) => user.name))

exercises.title: map or flatMap?
hints: Read the type error. Effect<Effect<User>> means an Effect is wrapped inside another.
map wraps the function's result. When that result is already an Effect, use flatMap.

exercises.title: Effect.gen
hints: Inside the generator, write yield* before an effect to get its result.
const id = yield* userId; const user = yield* loadUser(id); return user.name

exercises.title: Many steps, plain code in between
hints: Yield each effect into a variable, then use ordinary arithmetic.
const price = yield* priceOf(sku); const qty = yield* quantityOf(sku); return price * qty

exercises.title: if and for inside a generator
hints: Use a normal for...of loop and yield* inside it.
let total = 0; for (const sku of skus) { total += yield* stockOf(sku) }; return total < 10 ? "low" : "ok"

exercises.title: Forgetting yield*
hints: One of the two constants is still an Effect, not a number.
Add yield* in front of getA.

exercises.title: Peeking with tap
hints: tap runs an effect for its side effect and then passes the original value along.
Effect.tap((n) => Effect.sync(() => { seen.push(n) }))

exercises.title: Replacing the result
hints: Effect.as(value) ignores the old result and produces the new one.
saved.pipe(Effect.as("created")) and saved.pipe(Effect.asVoid)

exercises.title: Pairing results with zip
hints: zip runs both programs, one after the other, and gives you a pair.
Effect.zip(name, age)

exercises.title: Running a list of programs with all
hints: Effect.all accepts an array of effects.
Effect.all([name, age, admin])

exercises.title: all with named results
hints: Effect.all also accepts an object whose values are effects.
Effect.all({ name, age, admin })

exercises.title: Effect.forEach
hints: forEach takes the array first and the function second.
Effect.forEach(ids, loadName)

exercises.title: A failure stops the program
hints: Follow the generator from the top. What happens at the line that fails?
Steps after a failing yield* never run.

exercises.title: Effect.fn: functions that return programs
hints: Effect.fn("name") returns a function that accepts a generator function.
Effect.fn("priceWithTax")(function*(price: number) { const rate = yield* taxRate; return price + price * rate })

exercises.title: Building on smaller functions
hints: Call the smaller function and yield* its result, like any other effect.
const sub = yield* subtotal(unit, qty); return sub + shipping

exercises.title: Adding steps after the generator
hints: Effect.fn accepts more arguments after the generator. Each one is applied to the result.
Effect.fn("x")(function*..., Effect.map(...), Effect.tap(...))

exercises.title: fnUntraced
hints: It is the same shape as Effect.fn, without the name argument.
Effect.fnUntraced(function*(n: number) { ... })

exercises.title: Translate: a .then chain
hints: .then with a function returning a Promise is flatMap. With a plain value it is map.
fetchUser(id).pipe(Effect.flatMap((u) => fetchPosts(u.id)), Effect.map((posts) => posts.length))

exercises.title: Translate: an async function
hints: async becomes Effect.fn(...)(function*), and each await becomes yield*.
Keep the for loop and the ternary exactly as they are.

exercises.title: Translate: Promise.all
hints: The fixed list becomes Effect.all. The list built by map becomes Effect.forEach.
Effect.all([loadA, loadB]) and Effect.forEach(ids, load)

exercises.title: Capstone: a receipt
hints: Look up every price with forEach, then add them up with plain code.
Effect.all([Effect.forEach(skus, lookupPrice), taxRate]) gets the prices and the rate together.

exercises.title: Reading the success type
hints: Look at what the generator returns. It is a template string.
Change `Answer` to string.

exercises.title: Reading the error type
hints: Find the line that fails. What type does its argument have?
Change `Failure` to string.

exercises.title: Reading the requirements
hints: The generator yields Mailer. That is what the program asks for.
Change `Needs` to Mailer.

exercises.title: All three slots
hints: Each annotation must describe A, then E, then R. Use never for a slot that is empty.
fail("x") has A = never and E = string. The mailer program needs Mailer and finishes with a string.

exercises.title: Errors add up
hints: Yielding two effects that fail differently gives you both failures.
Change `Failure` to "timeout" | 404.

exercises.title: Changing the error with mapError
hints: mapError is to E what map is to A.
lookup.pipe(Effect.mapError((e) => new Error(`user ${e}`)))

exercises.title: Giving up on an error with orDie
hints: orDie removes the error from the type. The error becomes a crash.
parse(s).pipe(Effect.orDie)

exercises.title: Turning failure into a value with exit
hints: Effect.exit(program) wraps the outcome, so the new program cannot fail.
Effect.exit(risky)

exercises.title: Providing a service
hints: A program with a requirement cannot be run until the requirement is satisfied.
program.pipe(Effect.provideService(Mailer, { send: ... })) before running.

exercises.title: Providing one of two services
hints: Provide only Db. Mailer stays in R.
program.pipe(Effect.provideService(Db, { find: ... }))

exercises.title: runSync cannot wait
hints: Read the error. The program has to wait, so it cannot finish synchronously.
Use Effect.runPromise and await it.

exercises.title: Writing the whole signature
hints: Look at the body. What does it succeed with, how can it fail, and what does it yield*?
Effect.Effect<User, "not found", Users>

exercises.title: Stating the contract with fn.Return
hints: The annotation promises the error is exactly "divide by zero". But Effect.fail("...") widens its argument to string.
Write the failure as Effect.fail("divide by zero" as const).

exercises.title: Accepting effects that can fail
hints: The parameter type says the task never fails, but you pass one that can.
Widen the parameter: Effect.Effect<number, string>

exercises.title: Capstone: a function with a full signature
hints: Yield both services, look the user up, fail when there is no email, otherwise send.
Annotate the generator with Effect.fn.Return<"notified", "no such user", Db | Mailer>, and fail with "no such user" as const.

exercises.title: Errors are values with a tag
hints: A tagged error class extends Data.TaggedError("Name"). The type argument lists the fields.
class Forbidden extends Data.TaggedError("Forbidden")<{ readonly user: string }> {}

exercises.title: Failing with a tagged error
hints: Look the name up first. Fail when it is missing, succeed with a user when it is found.
const name = names.get(id); return name === undefined ? Effect.fail(new NotFound({ id })) : Effect.succeed({ id, name })

exercises.title: Yielding an error
hints: Compare amount with balance. Fail with the shortfall, otherwise return what is left.
if (amount > balance) return yield* new Insufficient({ needed: amount - balance })

exercises.title: Recovering with catch
hints: Effect.catch takes a function from the error to a new Effect.
parsePort(input).pipe(Effect.catch(() => Effect.succeed(3000)))

exercises.title: A handler can fail too
hints: The handler returns an Effect, so it can choose between succeed and fail.
Effect.catch(() => key in cache ? Effect.succeed(cache[key]) : Effect.fail(new Unavailable({ key })))

exercises.title: Handling one kind of error
hints: catchTag takes the tag first and the handler second.
lookup(id).pipe(Effect.catchTag("NotFound", () => Effect.succeed("anonymous")))

exercises.title: What is left after catchTag
hints: catchTag removes the tag it handled. Which tag does it handle here?
The program handles "NotFound", so only Denied remains.

exercises.title: Several tags, one handler
hints: Give catchTag an array of tags. The handler receives the union of those errors.
Effect.catchTag(["NotFound", "Denied"], (e) => Effect.succeed(`recovered from ${e._tag}`))

exercises.title: A handler per tag
hints: catchTags takes one object. Each key is a tag, each value is that tag's handler.
Effect.catchTags({ NotFound: () => ..., Denied: (e) => ..., Timeout: (e) => ... })

exercises.title: Handling errors that match a condition
hints: catchIf takes a predicate on the error, then a handler.
get(status).pipe(Effect.catchIf((e) => e.status === 404, () => Effect.succeed("")))

exercises.title: A default when you do not care why
hints: orElseSucceed takes a function that returns the default value.
parseCount(s).pipe(Effect.orElseSucceed(() => 0))

exercises.title: Handling both outcomes at once
hints: match takes an object with onFailure and onSuccess.
Effect.match({ onFailure: (e) => ..., onSuccess: (name) => ... })

exercises.title: Watching failures go by
hints: tapError is to the error what tap is to the result.
lookup(id).pipe(Effect.tapError((e) => Effect.sync(() => { seen.push(e._tag) })))

exercises.title: Keep the original error as cause
hints: Give catch the raw value and store it in the error: new DbError({ cause }).
catch: (cause) => new DbError({ cause })

exercises.title: Failure as data with result
hints: yield* Effect.result(program) inside a generator. It never fails.
outcome._tag === "Success" ? outcome.success : outcome.failure

exercises.title: Best effort with ignore
hints: Effect.ignore is a value you pass to pipe, not a function you call.
sendMetrics.pipe(Effect.ignore)

exercises.title: Validating with filterOrFail
hints: filterOrFail takes a predicate, then a function that builds the error.
Effect.succeed(age).pipe(Effect.filterOrFail((n) => n >= 18, (n) => new TooYoung({ age: n })))

exercises.title: Collecting failures instead of stopping
hints: partition takes the items and a function that returns an Effect for each.
Effect.partition(ns, validate)

exercises.title: Failures and defects
hints: Bad user input is expected, so it is a failure. An impossible state is a bug, so it is a defect.
Effect.fail(new InvalidInput({ field: "email" })) and Effect.die("unreachable state")

exercises.title: What does a throw become?
hints: Nobody declared these throws in E, except one of the three.
sync and gen: the throw is a defect. try: the throw is turned into a failure by catch.

exercises.title: try/catch does not catch failures
hints: A failing effect does not throw an exception, so the catch block never runs.
Drop the try/catch and use Effect.catch on the effect itself.

exercises.title: catch does not see defects
hints: Use catchDefect. Its handler receives the defect as unknown.
bug.pipe(Effect.catchDefect((defect) => Effect.succeed(`recovered from: ${String(defect)}`)))

exercises.title: orDie for things that cannot happen
hints: Both are the same call: pipe the parse into Effect.orDie.
parseHex("000000").pipe(Effect.orDie)

exercises.title: Looking inside a Cause
hints: catchCause sees everything, including defects. The handler receives the whole Cause.
cause.reasons.some(Cause.isDieReason) asks: is there a defect in here?

exercises.title: Reading an Exit
hints: Exit.match takes the exit, then an object with onSuccess and onFailure.
onFailure receives the Cause. Its reasons are in cause.reasons.

exercises.title: Errors with reasons
hints: catchReason takes the parent tag, then the reason tag, then a handler for that reason.
Effect.catchReason("AiError", "RateLimited", (reason) => Effect.succeed(`retry in ${reason.retryAfter}s`))

exercises.title: Translate: Error subclasses and instanceof
hints: Handle the two known errors with catchTags. Leave Crash alone, like the final throw e did.
load(id).pipe(Effect.map((name) => `hello ${name}`), Effect.catchTags({ NotFound: ..., Denied: ... }))

exercises.title: Translate: .catch and two-argument .then
hints: .catch(() => 0) ignores the error: orElseSucceed. .then(onOk, onErr) handles both: match.
Effect.orElseSucceed(() => 0) and Effect.match({ onFailure: () => "n/a", onSuccess: (p) => `$${p}` })

exercises.title: Capstone: placing an order
hints: placeOrder: look up the stock, fail with OutOfStock when short, then charge the price times the quantity.
placeOrder(sku, qty).pipe(Effect.catchTags({ UnknownSku: ..., OutOfStock: ..., PaymentDeclined: ... }))

exercises.title: Maybe there is a value
hints: Return Option.some(value) when you find one, Option.none() when you do not.
for (const n of ns) { if (n % 2 === 0) return Option.some(n) } return Option.none()

exercises.title: Asking an Option what it holds
hints: isSome narrows the type, so inside the true branch you can read .value.
Option.isSome(o) ? `value ${o.value}` : "nothing", and Option.isNone(o) for the second function.

exercises.title: From null and undefined to Option
hints: fromNullishOr takes any value. null and undefined become none, everything else becomes some.
Option.fromNullishOr(prices.get(sku))

exercises.title: Transforming an Option
hints: Options have .pipe just like Effects. map changes the value inside, if there is one.
price.pipe(Option.map((p) => p * 2)) and o.pipe(Option.getOrElse(() => 0))

exercises.title: Handling both cases with match
hints: match takes an object with onNone and onSome.
price.pipe(Option.match({ onNone: () => "no price", onSome: (p) => `$${p}` }))

exercises.title: Chaining lookups with flatMap
hints: Each step returns an Option, so use flatMap, not map.
findUser(id).pipe(Option.flatMap((u) => u.address), Option.flatMap((a) => a.city))

exercises.title: Filtering and falling back
hints: filter turns a some into none when the predicate is false.
age.pipe(Option.filter((a) => a >= 18)) and primary.pipe(Option.orElse(() => backup))

exercises.title: All or nothing
hints: Option.all takes an array (or an object) of Options.
Option.all([first, last]) and Option.all({ first, last })

exercises.title: From Option to Effect
hints: Effect.fromOption turns none into a failure. Then rename the failure with mapError.
Effect.fromOption(findUser(id)).pipe(Effect.mapError(() => new NotFound({ id })))

exercises.title: Failure to Option
hints: Effect.option is a value you pass to pipe, like Effect.ignore.
parseAge(s).pipe(Effect.option)

exercises.title: Result: success or failure as a plain value
hints: Return Result.fail(message) for the bad case and Result.succeed(value) otherwise.
b === 0 ? Result.fail("divide by zero") : Result.succeed(a / b)

exercises.title: Transforming and reading a Result
hints: Result has .pipe too. map changes the success value only.
r.pipe(Result.map((n) => n * 2)) and r.pipe(Result.match({ onFailure: ..., onSuccess: ... }))

exercises.title: Catching a throw into a Result
hints: Same shape as Effect.try: an object with try and catch.
Result.try({ try: () => JSON.parse(input) as unknown, catch: () => "invalid json" })

exercises.title: Chaining fallible steps
hints: Each step returns a Result, so chain them with flatMap.
parse(s).pipe(Result.flatMap(positive), Result.flatMap(even))

exercises.title: Moving between Result and Effect
hints: fromResult lifts a Result into an Effect. Effect.result goes the other way.
Effect.fromResult(parse(s)) and Effect.result(program)

exercises.title: Safe first and last
hints: Import the Array module under a new name so it does not hide the global Array.
[Arr.head(ns), Arr.last(ns)]

exercises.title: Finding an element
hints: findFirst takes the array and a predicate, and returns an Option.
Arr.findFirst(people, (p) => p.age >= 18)

exercises.title: Grouping
hints: groupBy takes the items and a function that returns the group key as a string.
Arr.groupBy(words, (w) => String(w.length))

exercises.title: Sorting with an Order
hints: Arr.sort takes an Order, and Order.Number or Order.String are ready-made ones.
pipe(ns, Arr.sort(Order.Number))

exercises.title: Sorting records by a field
hints: mapInput adapts an Order for numbers into an Order for people, by saying how to get the number.
const byAge = Order.mapInput(Order.Number, (p: Person) => p.age)

exercises.title: Deduplicating and chunking
hints: Both take the array first. chunksOf also takes the chunk size.
Arr.dedupe(ns) and Arr.chunksOf(ns, 2)

exercises.title: Splitting in two
hints: The function returns a Result for each item: succeed for one group, fail for the other.
Arr.partition(ns, (n) => n % 2 === 0 ? Result.succeed(n) : Result.fail(n))

exercises.title: Records: get and map
hints: Import Record under an alias for the same reason as Array.
Rec.get(prices, sku) and Rec.map(prices, (p) => p * 2)

exercises.title: Records: from entries, filter, keys
hints: fromEntries takes an array of [key, value] pairs.
Rec.fromEntries(pairs), Rec.filter(prices, (p) => p > 5), Rec.keys(prices)

exercises.title: Equal by value
hints: Two Point objects are different objects, so === is false. Data.Class makes them equal by value.
class Point extends Data.Class<{ readonly x: number; readonly y: number }> {}

exercises.title: A union with tags
hints: Each constructor takes the fields of that case. The tag is added for you.
[Circle({ radius: 1 }), Square({ side: 2 }), Circle({ radius: 3 })] and shapes.filter($is("Circle")).length

exercises.title: Match by tag
hints: Start with Match.type<Shape>(), then one Match.tag per case, then Match.exhaustive.
Match.type<Shape>().pipe(Match.tag("Circle", (c) => ...), Match.tag("Square", (s) => ...), Match.exhaustive)

exercises.title: Exhaustive means every case
hints: Read the type error. A case of the union has no handler.
Add Match.tag("Triangle", (t) => t.base * t.height / 2) before Match.exhaustive.

exercises.title: Match on values and types
hints: Match.value(input) starts a match on one value. Each Match.when has a pattern and a handler.
Match.value(input).pipe(Match.when(Match.string, (s) => ...), Match.when(Match.number, (n) => ...), Match.orElse(() => "something else"))

exercises.title: Durations
hints: Build each part with Duration.minutes and Duration.seconds, then add them with Duration.sum.
Duration.toMillis(Duration.sum(Duration.minutes(1), Duration.seconds(30)))

exercises.title: Comparing and parsing durations
hints: fromInput accepts the same text Effect.sleep accepts, and returns an Option.
Duration.fromInput(input).pipe(Option.map((d) => Duration.isGreaterThan(d, limit)), Option.getOrElse(() => false))

exercises.title: Combining predicates
hints: and, or and not combine predicates the way && || ! combine booleans.
Predicate.and(isEven, isSmall), Predicate.or(Predicate.isString, Predicate.isNumber), Predicate.not(Predicate.isString)

exercises.title: Translate: optional chaining
hints: Convert each nullable step into an Option, chain with flatMap, and finish with getOrElse.
Option.fromNullishOr(user).pipe(Option.flatMap((u) => Option.fromNullishOr(u.address)), Option.flatMap((a) => Option.fromNullishOr(a.city)), Option.getOrElse(() => "unknown"))

exercises.title: Translate: a switch on a tag
hints: Each case of the switch becomes a Match.tag. The default that never happens becomes Match.exhaustive.
Match.type<Event>().pipe(Match.tag("Click", ...), Match.tag("Key", ...), Match.tag("Scroll", ...), Match.exhaustive)

exercises.title: Capstone: an inventory file
hints: parseLine: split on ":", turn the quantity into an Option, keep it only if it is a whole number, then match to a Result.
summarize: map the lines with parseLine, then Arr.getSuccesses and Arr.getFailures split the Results.

exercises.title: Defining a service
hints: A service class extends Context.Service<Self, Shape>() and then takes a string id.
class Greeter extends Context.Service<Greeter, { readonly greet: (name: string) => string }>()("Greeter") {}

exercises.title: Using a service
hints: Yield the service to get it, then call its methods. Yield each method call too, since it returns an Effect.
const logger = yield* Logger; yield* logger.log("start"); yield* logger.log("end"); return "done"

exercises.title: Implementations are plain objects
hints: Clock.of(...) checks that your object has the right shape.
Clock.of({ now: () => 1000 }), and for the ticking one keep a counter outside: () => (tickCount += 1)

exercises.title: The use shortcuts
hints: useSync takes a function from the service to a plain value. use takes one that returns an Effect.
Settings.useSync((s) => s.port) and Settings.use((s) => s.describe())

exercises.title: Layers: recipes for services
hints: Layer.succeed takes the service class and an implementation.
Layer.succeed(Logger, Logger.of({ log: ... })) and program.pipe(Effect.provide(loggerLayer))

exercises.title: Layers that run setup code
hints: Layer.effect takes the service class and an Effect that produces the implementation.
Layer.effect(Counter, Effect.sync(() => { let n = 0; return Counter.of({ next: () => ++n }) }))

exercises.title: The layer lives on the service
hints: Inside the class body, write a static property. You can refer to the class by name.
static readonly layer = Layer.succeed(Mailer, Mailer.of({ send: (to) => Effect.succeed(`sent to ${to}`) }))

exercises.title: Reading a Layer's type
hints: Layer<ROut, E, RIn>: what it provides, how building it can fail, what it needs to be built.
It provides Users, can fail with NotConnected, and needs Db.

exercises.title: Feeding a layer its dependencies
hints: usersLayer needs Db, and dbLayer provides Db.
usersLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(dbLayer))

exercises.title: Keeping the dependency visible
hints: provideMerge feeds the dependency like provide does, and also keeps it in the output.
usersLayer.pipe(Layer.provideMerge(dbLayer))

exercises.title: Combining independent layers
hints: merge takes two layers. mergeAll takes any number.
Layer.merge(clockLayer, loggerLayer) and Layer.mergeAll(clockLayer, loggerLayer, idsLayer)

exercises.title: Provide from the outside in
hints: The program needs Users. Users needs Db. Which layer must be provided first?
Provide usersLayer first (it satisfies the program), then dbLayer (it satisfies usersLayer). Or combine with Layer.provide.

exercises.title: A layer is built once per provide
hints: Inside ONE provide, a layer that two others depend on is built once and shared.
Two separate Effect.provide calls each build their own copy.

exercises.title: Asking for a separate copy
hints: Layer.fresh(layer) wraps a layer so it is built again instead of shared.
bFromBase.pipe(Layer.provide(Layer.fresh(base)))

exercises.title: Services with a default
hints: Context.Reference takes the value type, an id, and an options object with defaultValue.
Context.Reference<"quiet" | "loud">("Verbosity", { defaultValue: () => "quiet" as const })

exercises.title: An optional service
hints: Effect.serviceOption(Metrics) gives an Option. Check it with Option.isSome.
const metrics = yield* Effect.serviceOption(Metrics); if (Option.isSome(metrics)) yield* metrics.value.count("work")

exercises.title: Changing a service for part of a program
hints: updateService takes the service class and a function from the current implementation to a new one.
greet.pipe(Effect.updateService(Settings, (s) => ({ ...s, prefix: "child" })))

exercises.title: The make option
hints: this.make is the effect you gave to the class. Layer.effect(this, this.make) builds a layer from it.
static readonly layer = Layer.effect(this, this.make)

exercises.title: One program, two implementations
hints: Both layers provide Mailer. The test one records the address in `outbox`.
Layer.succeed(Mailer, Mailer.of({ send: (to) => Effect.sync(() => { outbox.push(to); return `recorded ${to}` }) }))

exercises.title: Partial fakes with Layer.mock
hints: Layer.mock(Service) returns a function. Call it with only the members you want to implement.
Layer.mock(Users)({ find: (id) => Effect.succeed(`user-${id}`) })

exercises.title: Layers can fail
hints: Fail inside the Effect you give to Layer.effect, before returning the service.
if (url === "") return yield* new ConnectionFailed({ url })

exercises.title: Translate: constructor injection
hints: The constructor parameters become things you yield* at the top of the layer's generator.
Inside Layer.effect(UserService, Effect.gen(...)): const db = yield* Db; const mailer = yield* Mailer; then define register.

exercises.title: Translate: a global config object
hints: endpoint yields Settings and builds the url. The two layers differ only in the apiUrl they provide.
Layer.succeed(Settings, Settings.of({ apiUrl: "https://prod.example.com" }))

exercises.title: Capstone: wiring an app
hints: Users.layer needs Db and Mailer: yield both, then build welcome. appLayer feeds it the two dependency layers.
Users.layer.pipe(Layer.provide(Layer.mergeAll(dbLayer, mailerLayer)))

exercises.title: Cleanup that always runs
hints: ensuring takes the cleanup Effect, not a function.
task.pipe(Effect.ensuring(cleanup))

exercises.title: Reacting to how a program ended
hints: The function you give to onExit receives the Exit. Exit.isSuccess tells you which way it went.
task.pipe(Effect.onExit((exit) => Effect.sync(() => { log.push(Exit.isSuccess(exit) ? "succeeded" : "failed") })))

exercises.title: acquireUseRelease
hints: Three arguments, in order: how to get it, what to do with it, how to give it back.
Effect.acquireUseRelease(openFile, (file) => read(file), (file) => file.close())

exercises.title: What happens when use fails?
hints: Follow the three phases. Does a failure in use skip the release?
open, then use (which fails), then close. The release still runs.

exercises.title: Resources that live in a scope
hints: acquireRelease takes the acquire Effect and a release function. scoped marks where the resources are released.
Effect.acquireRelease(open, () => close), then Effect.scoped(Effect.gen(...)) around the code that uses it.

exercises.title: Scope in the type
hints: acquireRelease leaves a promise to release later. That promise is a requirement: Scope.
Needs is Scope.Scope. After Effect.scoped, nothing is required.

exercises.title: Released in reverse order
hints: Resources are released in the opposite order they were acquired, like a stack.
open a, open b, working, then close b, close a.

exercises.title: Registering cleanup by hand
hints: addFinalizer takes a function that returns the cleanup Effect. It must run inside a scope.
yield* Effect.addFinalizer(() => Effect.sync(() => { log.push("cleanup") }))

exercises.title: Finalizers see how the scope ended
hints: The finalizer receives the Exit of the scoped block. Its _tag is "Success" or "Failure".
The first program succeeds and the second fails.

exercises.title: A layer that owns a resource
hints: Give Layer.effect an acquireRelease. The layer handles the scope for you.
Layer.effect(Db, Effect.acquireRelease(connect, () => disconnect))

exercises.title: Closing a scope yourself
hints: The scope is made and used, but nothing ever closes it.
await Effect.runPromise(Scope.close(scope, Exit.void))

exercises.title: Translate: try/finally
hints: The open is the acquire, the body of try is use, the finally block is release.
Effect.acquireUseRelease(open(path), (file) => file.readLine(), (file) => file.close())

exercises.title: Translate: nested try/finally
hints: Two acquireRelease calls in one scoped generator replace the nesting.
Effect.scoped(Effect.gen(function*() { const db = yield* acquireDb; const cache = yield* acquireCache; return yield* work(db, cache) }))

exercises.title: Capstone: startup and shutdown order
hints: The server layer needs Db, so yield Db inside it. Build it with acquireRelease like the db layer.
serverLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(dbLayer)) makes a layer that needs nothing.

exercises.title: Running something in the background
hints: forkChild starts the work and gives you a Fiber straight away. Fiber.join waits for its result.
const fiber = yield* Effect.forkChild(slowDouble(21)); ...; const doubled = yield* Fiber.join(fiber)

exercises.title: Who goes first?
hints: forkChild returns immediately. The child has to sleep before it logs.
forked, then the child finishes, then joined.

exercises.title: join or await?
hints: Fiber.await gives you the Exit and never fails. Fiber.join fails if the fiber failed.
outcome: fork, then yield* Fiber.await(fiber). joined: fork, then yield* Fiber.join(fiber).

exercises.title: Stopping a fiber
hints: Fork Effect.never, let it start with Effect.yieldNow, interrupt it, then await its Exit.
const fiber = yield* Effect.forkChild(Effect.never); yield* Effect.yieldNow; yield* Fiber.interrupt(fiber); return yield* Fiber.await(fiber)

exercises.title: Cleaning up when interrupted
hints: onInterrupt takes a function returning the cleanup Effect. It runs only on interruption.
Effect.never.pipe(Effect.onInterrupt(() => Effect.sync(() => { log.push("cleanup") })))

exercises.title: Protecting a critical section
hints: The job is cut short by the interrupt. Mark it so interruption waits for it.
const task = Effect.uninterruptible(job)

exercises.title: Children end with their parent
hints: A child started with forkChild cannot outlive the fiber that forked it.
child started, parent done, then the child is interrupted as the parent finishes.

exercises.title: Outliving the parent
hints: forkDetach starts a fiber that is not tied to the parent.
yield* Effect.forkDetach(job); return "started"

exercises.title: A fiber that lives as long as a scope
hints: forkScoped ties the fiber to the current Scope, so the type needs Scope.Scope in R.
Effect.gen(function*() { yield* Effect.forkScoped(worker) })

exercises.title: Running things at the same time
hints: Effect.all takes an options object as its second argument.
Effect.all([...], { concurrency: "unbounded" })

exercises.title: At most N at a time
hints: forEach takes the options object as its third argument.
Effect.forEach(ns, work, { concurrency: 2 })

exercises.title: The first one wins
hints: race takes two effects. The loser is interrupted.
Effect.race(slow, fast)

exercises.title: Giving up after a while
hints: timeout takes a duration and adds a TimeoutError to the error channel.
slow.pipe(Effect.timeout("5 millis"), Effect.catchTag("TimeoutError", () => Effect.succeed("gave up")))

exercises.title: A fallback on timeout
hints: timeoutOrElse takes one object: the duration and an orElse function.
slow.pipe(Effect.timeoutOrElse({ duration: "5 millis", orElse: () => Effect.succeed("fallback") }))

exercises.title: Mutable state with Ref
hints: Ref.make creates the Ref with an initial value. get reads it, set replaces it.
const status = yield* Ref.make("draft"); const before = yield* Ref.get(status); yield* Ref.set(status, "published")

exercises.title: Updating a Ref
hints: update takes a function from the old value to the new one. updateAndGet also returns the new value.
yield* Ref.update(counter, (n) => n + 1) three times, then return yield* Ref.updateAndGet(counter, (n) => n + 10)

exercises.title: Reading and changing in one step
hints: modify's function returns a pair: [the value to hand back, the new state].
Ref.modify(ref, (n) => [n, n + 1])

exercises.title: Many fibers, one Ref
hints: Create the Ref, run n updates with forEach and concurrency "unbounded", then read it.
Effect.forEach(Array.from({ length: n }), () => Ref.update(counter, (x) => x + 1), { concurrency: "unbounded" })

exercises.title: Waiting for a signal
hints: A Deferred starts empty. One fiber awaits it, another completes it.
const signal = yield* Deferred.make<string>(); fork Deferred.await(signal); later yield* Deferred.succeed(signal, "go")

exercises.title: A signal that failed
hints: Deferred.make takes a second type argument for the error. fail completes it with a failure.
const d = yield* Deferred.make<string, string>(); yield* Deferred.fail(d, "cancelled"); return yield* Deferred.await(d)

exercises.title: A gate that opens
hints: A Latch starts closed when you pass false. Fibers that await it wait until it is opened.
const gate = yield* Latch.make(false); ...Latch.await(gate)...; yield* Latch.open(gate)

exercises.title: One at a time
hints: Make a semaphore with one permit, then wrap each job so it holds a permit while it runs.
const sem = yield* Semaphore.make(1); const guarded = Semaphore.withPermits(sem, 1)(job)

exercises.title: Queues
hints: Create the queue, put things in with offer or offerAll, take them out with take. First in, first out.
yield* Queue.offer(queue, 1); yield* Queue.offerAll(queue, [2, 3]); then Queue.take three times

exercises.title: A full queue makes the producer wait
hints: Queue.bounded(1) holds one item. The second offer cannot finish until somebody takes.
Only the first offer completed, so the counter is 1.

exercises.title: Producer and consumer
hints: Fork the consumer first so it is already waiting, then produce, then join the consumer.
The consumer takes three values and adds them. The producer offers 1, 2, 3.

exercises.title: A queue that drops
hints: dropping(n) refuses new values when full. offer tells you whether it was accepted.
const accepted = [yield* Queue.offer(q, 1), ...]; const kept = yield* Queue.takeAll(q)

exercises.title: Broadcasting with PubSub
hints: Subscribe before you publish: a subscriber only receives messages published after it subscribed.
const s1 = yield* PubSub.subscribe(hub); const s2 = yield* PubSub.subscribe(hub); yield* PubSub.publish(hub, "hi"); PubSub.take(s1)

exercises.title: Translate: Promise.all and Promise.race
hints: Promise.all becomes Effect.all with concurrency "unbounded". Promise.race becomes Effect.race.
Effect.all([loadUser, loadPosts], { concurrency: "unbounded" }) and Effect.race(mirrorA, mirrorB)

exercises.title: Translate: a parallel limit
hints: p-limit's limit(2) is the concurrency option of forEach.
Effect.forEach(urls, download, { concurrency: 2 })

exercises.title: Translate: AbortController
hints: tryPromise passes an AbortSignal to your try function. Interrupting the fiber aborts that signal.
Effect.tryPromise({ try: (signal) => slowFetch(signal), catch: () => "failed" })

exercises.title: Capstone: a pool of workers
hints: Put the jobs in the queue, fork two workers that each take half of them, join both, read the Ref.
Each worker: for (let i = 0; i < perWorker; i++) { const job = yield* Queue.take(queue); yield* Ref.update(total, (n) => n + job * 2) }

exercises.title: Checking unknown data
hints: Schema.decodeUnknownSync(schema) gives you a function from unknown to the schema's type.
const parseName = Schema.decodeUnknownSync(Schema.String)

exercises.title: Describing an object
hints: Schema.Struct takes an object whose values are schemas, one per field.
Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.String, age: Schema.Number })

exercises.title: What a failed decode throws
hints: Wrap the decode in try/catch. A SchemaError means the input was bad; anything else is unexpected.
catch (error) { if (Schema.isSchemaError(error)) return "invalid"; throw error }

exercises.title: Decoding without exceptions: Option
hints: decodeUnknownOption returns some(value) when the input fits and none when it does not.
Schema.decodeUnknownOption(Person)(input)

exercises.title: Decoding inside Effect
hints: decodeUnknownEffect fails with a SchemaError, whose tag is "SchemaError".
decodePerson(input).pipe(Effect.map((p) => `hello ${p.name}`), Effect.catchTag("SchemaError", () => Effect.succeed("invalid person")))

exercises.title: A type guard from a schema
hints: Schema.is(Person) is a function you can call in an if. Inside the branch TypeScript knows the shape.
Schema.is(Person)(input) ? `person ${input.name}` : "not a person"

exercises.title: Optional fields
hints: optionalKey: the key may be absent. optional: the key may be absent or hold undefined.
nickname: Schema.optionalKey(Schema.String), age: Schema.optional(Schema.Number)

exercises.title: null is a value too
hints: NullOr wraps another schema and also allows null.
Schema.Struct({ id: Schema.Number, deletedAt: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String) })

exercises.title: Arrays
hints: Schema.Array takes the schema of one element.
Schema.Array(Schema.Number)

exercises.title: Records with any keys
hints: Schema.Record takes a schema for the keys and a schema for the values.
Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Number)

exercises.title: Tuples
hints: Schema.Tuple takes an array of schemas, one per position.
Schema.Tuple([Schema.Number, Schema.Number])

exercises.title: Exact values
hints: Literal is for one exact value, Literals for a set of them.
Schema.Literal("v1") and Schema.Literals(["draft", "published"])

exercises.title: One of several shapes
hints: Union takes an array of schemas. The input must fit at least one.
Schema.Union([Schema.String, Schema.Number])

exercises.title: Tagged structs
hints: TaggedStruct takes the tag first and the fields second, and adds the _tag field for you.
Schema.TaggedStruct("Circle", { radius: Schema.Number })

exercises.title: Rules for strings
hints: Put the rules inside .check(...) on the base schema. You can give it several.
Schema.String.check(Schema.isMinLength(3), Schema.isMaxLength(12), Schema.isPattern(/^[a-z0-9_]+$/))

exercises.title: Rules for numbers
hints: isInt() takes no arguments. isBetween takes an object with minimum and maximum.
Schema.Number.check(Schema.isInt(), Schema.isBetween({ minimum: 0, maximum: 130 }))

exercises.title: Your own error message
hints: Most checks take an options object as the last argument. message is one of its fields.
Schema.isGreaterThan(0, { message: "must be positive" })

exercises.title: A rule of your own
hints: makeFilter takes a function from the value to: undefined when it is fine, or a message when it is not.
Schema.makeFilter((n: number) => (n % 2 === 0 ? undefined : "must be even"))

exercises.title: Branded types
hints: brand is applied with pipe, and takes the name of the brand.
Schema.String.pipe(Schema.brand("UserId"))

exercises.title: The brand protects you
hints: loadUser wants a UserId, not any string. Turn the string into a UserId first.
loadUser(Schema.decodeUnknownSync(UserId)("u_7"))

exercises.title: Decoding changes the value
hints: Decode with decodeUnknownSync and the other direction with encodeSync, both on NumberFromString.
const parseQty = Schema.decodeUnknownSync(Schema.NumberFromString); const formatQty = Schema.encodeSync(Schema.NumberFromString)

exercises.title: Type and Encoded
hints: qty and at change during decoding. The Type holds a number and a Date, the Encoded form holds strings.
Type: { qty: number; at: Date }. Encoded: { qty: string; at: string }.

exercises.title: There and back again
hints: encodeSync turns each field back to its Encoded form. The number becomes a string, the Date an ISO string.

exercises.title: Your own conversion
hints: transform takes a decode function and an encode function. They must undo each other.
Schema.Finite.pipe(Schema.decode(SchemaTransformation.transform({ decode: (m: number) => m / 1000, encode: (k: number) => k * 1000 })))

exercises.title: From one shape to another
hints: decodeTo takes the target schema and a transformation whose decode and encode convert between the two shapes.
Schema.decodeTo(Schema.Struct({ age: Schema.Number }), SchemaTransformation.transform({ decode: ..., encode: ... }))

exercises.title: Cleaning input
hints: Both are ready-made transformations. Attach each with Schema.decode.
Schema.String.pipe(Schema.decode(SchemaTransformation.trim()), Schema.decode(SchemaTransformation.toLowerCase()))

exercises.title: A default when a field is missing
hints: Start from an optionalKey, then pipe it into withDecodingDefaultKey with an Effect that produces the default.
Schema.optionalKey(Schema.Number).pipe(Schema.withDecodingDefaultKey(Effect.succeed(3)))

exercises.title: Defaults when building values
hints: Settings.make({ host }) fails to compile because retries is required. Give retries a constructor default.
retries: Schema.Number.pipe(Schema.withConstructorDefault(Effect.succeed(3)))

exercises.title: make checks the rules too
hints: .make throws when a rule fails, so wrap it in try/catch.
try { Adult.make({ name, age }); return `registered ${name}` } catch { return "rejected" }

exercises.title: Schemas that are classes
hints: The class has no fields, so this.age does not exist. Extend Schema.Class and list the fields there.
class Person extends Schema.Class<Person>("Person")({ name: Schema.String, age: Schema.Number }) { ... }

exercises.title: Classes with a tag
hints: TaggedClass works like Class, but takes the tag as its first argument and adds the _tag field.
class Deposit extends Schema.TaggedClass<Deposit>()("Deposit", { amount: Schema.Number }) {}

exercises.title: Errors defined by schemas
hints: It has the same shape as TaggedClass: Schema.TaggedError<Self>()(tag, fields).
class InsufficientFunds extends Schema.TaggedError<InsufficientFunds>()("InsufficientFunds", { needed: Schema.Number }) {}

exercises.title: Schemas for JSON text
hints: Give fromJsonString the schema of the value INSIDE the JSON.
Schema.fromJsonString(Person)

exercises.title: null in the data, Option in the program
hints: OptionFromNullOr wraps the schema of the value that may be present.
Schema.OptionFromNullOr(Schema.String)

exercises.title: Reusing fields
hints: A Struct remembers its fields in .fields. fieldsAssign adds more.
Person.pipe(Schema.fieldsAssign({ company: Schema.String })) and Schema.Struct({ name: Person.fields.name })

exercises.title: Schemas that contain themselves
hints: The children field is an array of the schema you are defining. Wrap the self-reference in Schema.suspend.
children: Schema.Array(Schema.suspend((): Schema.Codec<Category> => Category))

exercises.title: Translate: a hand-written type guard
hints: The fields go into a Struct. The guard is Schema.is of that schema.
const User = Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.String, age: Schema.Number }); const isUser = Schema.is(User)

exercises.title: Translate: JSON.parse with a cast
hints: Decode the text with the schema from fromJsonString, using decodeUnknownEffect.
Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(Schema.fromJsonString(Config))(text)

exercises.title: Capstone: loading configuration
hints: Config: host is a string, port an integer from 1 to 65535, env is an optional "dev" or "prod" defaulting to "dev".
loadConfig decodes Schema.fromJsonString(Config) and mapErrors the SchemaError into a ConfigError with its message.

exercises.title: A stream is many values over time
hints: Stream.make takes the values. map and runCollect work like the ones you know.
Stream.make(1, 2, 3).pipe(Stream.map((n) => n * 2), Stream.runCollect)

exercises.title: Streams from collections
hints: fromIterable takes any array or iterable. range takes a start and an end, both included.
Stream.fromIterable(words).pipe(Stream.filter(...), Stream.runCollect) and Stream.range(1, 5).pipe(Stream.runCollect)

exercises.title: Taking part of a stream
hints: take keeps the first n values, drop skips them.
Stream.range(1, 10).pipe(Stream.drop(2), Stream.take(3), Stream.runCollect)

exercises.title: Streams can be infinite
hints: iterate takes a starting value and a function from the current value to the next.
Stream.iterate(1, (n) => n * 2).pipe(Stream.take(6), Stream.runCollect)

exercises.title: Only as much as needed
hints: tap runs an effect for each value as it passes, like Effect.tap. Only values that are pulled pass through it.
The stream stops after 3 values, so the tap sees 3.

exercises.title: Reducing a stream
hints: runFold takes a function that returns the starting value, and a function that combines.
Stream.runFold(() => 0, (total, n) => total + n), Stream.runSum, Stream.runCount

exercises.title: Doing something with every value
hints: runForEach takes a function returning an Effect for each value. runDrain runs the stream and discards values.
Stream.runForEach((n) => Effect.sync(() => { seen.push(n) })) and stream.pipe(Stream.tap(...), Stream.runDrain)

exercises.title: The first and last value
hints: Both give an Option, because the stream might be empty.
Stream.runHead and Stream.runLast

exercises.title: Effects for every value
hints: mapEffect is map with a function that returns an Effect. It runs one value at a time by default.
Stream.mapEffect(lookup, { concurrency: 3 })

exercises.title: One value, many values
hints: The function you give to flatMap returns a Stream. Everything it produces is emitted in place of the original value.
Stream.flatMap((n) => Stream.make(n, n * 10))

exercises.title: Joining streams
hints: concat plays one stream after the other. zip pairs values up and stops with the shorter stream.
Stream.concat(a, b) and Stream.zip(a, b)

exercises.title: Running totals
hints: scan works like fold, but emits every intermediate total, starting with the initial value.
Stream.scan(() => 0, (total: number, n: number) => total + n)

exercises.title: Stopping on a condition
hints: takeWhile stops BEFORE the first value that fails. takeUntil keeps the value that satisfies it.
Stream.takeWhile((n) => n < 4) and Stream.takeUntil((n) => n === 4)

exercises.title: Batching
hints: grouped takes the batch size. The last batch may be smaller.
Stream.grouped(2)

exercises.title: Generating from state
hints: unfold takes a seed and an effectful function returning [value, nextSeed], or undefined to stop.
Stream.unfold(1, (n) => Effect.succeed(n > 5 ? undefined : [n * n, n + 1] as const))

exercises.title: Paging through an API
hints: The step function gets the page number and returns [itemsOfThisPage, Option of the next page].
Stream.paginate(1, (page) => fetchPage(page).pipe(Effect.map((r) => [r.items, r.next] as const)))

exercises.title: A stream from one Effect
hints: fromEffect runs the effect once per pull when combined with forever.
Stream.fromEffect(readSensor).pipe(Stream.forever, Stream.take(3), Stream.runCollect)

exercises.title: Failures in a stream
hints: A failure ends the stream. Stream.catch replaces the rest of it with another stream.
source.pipe(Stream.catch(() => Stream.make(-1)))

exercises.title: Cleanup when a stream ends
hints: Stream.ensuring takes the cleanup Effect, like Effect.ensuring.
Stream.make(1, 2).pipe(Stream.ensuring(cleanup), Stream.runCollect)

exercises.title: A stream from a queue
hints: A stream ends when the queue is ended. The queue's error type must include Cause.Done.
const queue = yield* Queue.unbounded<number, Cause.Done>(); yield* Queue.offerAll(queue, [1, 2, 3]); yield* Queue.end(queue)

exercises.title: Bridging an event source
hints: The function receives a queue. Push values with Queue.offerUnsafe and close it with Queue.endUnsafe.
Stream.callback<number>((queue) => Effect.sync(() => { source.subscribe((n) => Queue.offerUnsafe(queue, n), () => Queue.endUnsafe(queue)) }))

exercises.title: Sinks: the consumer side
hints: Stream.run takes a Sink and runs the whole stream into it.
numbers.pipe(Stream.run(Sink.sum)) and numbers.pipe(Stream.run(Sink.collect<number>()))

exercises.title: Sinks that stop early
hints: Sink.take(n) consumes only n values and then finishes, so an endless stream is fine.
Stream.iterate(0, (n) => n + 1).pipe(Stream.run(Sink.take<number>(3)))

exercises.title: Your own sink
hints: Sink.reduce takes a function returning the start value and a function combining state and input.
Sink.reduce(() => 0, (longest: number, word: string) => Math.max(longest, word.length))

exercises.title: Merging streams
hints: merge runs both streams at the same time and emits values as they arrive.
Stream.merge(fast, slow)

exercises.title: Text in chunks
hints: Chunks of text arrive cut at arbitrary places. splitLines puts them back together into lines.
Stream.fromIterable(chunks).pipe(Stream.splitLines, Stream.runCollect)

exercises.title: Translate: an array pipeline
hints: Each array method has a stream twin. The final reduce becomes runSum.
Stream.fromIterable(orders).pipe(Stream.filter(...), Stream.map(...), Stream.runSum)

exercises.title: Translate: for await
hints: fromAsyncIterable takes the iterable and a function that turns a thrown error into your error type.
Stream.fromAsyncIterable(numbers(), () => "stream failed")

exercises.title: Capstone: summarizing a log
hints: Split chunks into lines, drop the empty ones, read the level as the first word, then fold into counts.
Stream.runFold(() => ({ info: 0, warn: 0, error: 0 }), (counts, level) => ({ ...counts, [level]: counts[level] + 1 }))

exercises.title: Trying again
hints: retry takes an options object. times says how many EXTRA attempts are allowed.
flaky.pipe(Effect.retry({ times: 3 }))

exercises.title: When retries run out
hints: times: 2 allows the first attempt and two retries. Count how many of them fail.
The task fails on attempts 1, 2 and 3. Three attempts are allowed, so no attempt succeeds.

exercises.title: Only retry what can get better
hints: while is a predicate on the error. Retry only when it returns true.
call.pipe(Effect.retry({ while: (e) => e._tag === "Timeout", times: 5 }))

exercises.title: Schedules
hints: recurs takes the number of repetitions.
const policy: Schedule.Schedule<number> = Schedule.recurs(3)

exercises.title: A clock you control
hints: adjust moves the test clock forward. Sleeping fibers wake up when their time comes.
yield* TestClock.adjust("1 hour")

exercises.title: Waiting between attempts
hints: Pass a schedule AND a limit to retry. spaced waits the same time before each retry.
task.pipe(Effect.retry({ schedule: Schedule.spaced("1 second"), times: 5 }))

exercises.title: Backing off
hints: exponential takes the first delay. Each following delay is twice as long.
task.pipe(Effect.retry({ schedule: Schedule.exponential("100 millis"), times: 5 }))

exercises.title: Limiting a schedule
hints: upTo takes an options object with times, duration, or both.
Schedule.exponential("100 millis").pipe(Schedule.upTo({ times: 3 }))

exercises.title: Doing it again, on success
hints: repeat takes the same kind of options as retry. times: 2 means two EXTRA runs.
tick.pipe(Effect.repeat({ times: 2 }))

exercises.title: Repeating until a condition
hints: until is a predicate on the SUCCESS value. Repeating stops when it returns true.
check.pipe(Effect.repeat({ until: (status) => status === "ready" }))

exercises.title: Repeating on a timer
hints: Give repeat a schedule for the pause and a limit for the count.
sample.pipe(Effect.repeat({ schedule: Schedule.spaced("1 second"), times: 2 }))

exercises.title: Testing a timeout without waiting
hints: Fork the guarded task, move the clock past the timeout, then join.
const fiber = yield* Effect.forkChild(guarded(slow)); yield* TestClock.adjust("1 minute"); return yield* Fiber.join(fiber)

exercises.title: Dates as values
hints: makeUnsafe throws on bad input. make returns an Option instead.
DateTime.makeUnsafe("2026-01-15T10:30:00Z"), DateTime.make(input), DateTime.formatIso(dt), DateTime.toEpochMillis(dt)

exercises.title: Adding and subtracting time
hints: add and subtract take an object such as { days: 20 }. startOf and endOf take a unit such as "month".
DateTime.add(start, { days: 20 }), DateTime.subtract(start, { weeks: 1 }), DateTime.startOf(start, "month")

exercises.title: Comparing and measuring
hints: isGreaterThan(a, b) asks whether a is later than b. distance gives a Duration.
DateTime.isGreaterThan(now, deadline) and Duration.toMillis(DateTime.distance(from, to))

exercises.title: The current time, as a dependency
hints: DateTime.now is an Effect. It reads the Clock, so a test can set the time.
const now = yield* DateTime.now; return DateTime.isGreaterThan(now, deadline)

exercises.title: Time zones
hints: makeZoned takes the input and an options object with a timeZone. It returns an Option.
DateTime.makeZoned(input, { timeZone: "Europe/Paris" }) and DateTime.formatIsoZoned(zoned)

exercises.title: Translate: setInterval
hints: Three polls means one run plus two repeats, one second apart.
poll.pipe(Effect.repeat({ schedule: Schedule.spaced("1 second"), times: 2 }), Effect.asVoid)

exercises.title: Translate: a retry loop with backoff
hints: The loop, the counter and the sleep all collapse into a schedule.
call.pipe(Effect.retry({ schedule: Schedule.exponential("100 millis"), times: 3 }))

exercises.title: Capstone: poll until ready
hints: Repeat the check every second until the status is "ready", then wrap the whole thing in a ten second timeout.

check.pipe(Effect.repeat({ schedule: Schedule.spaced("1 second"), until: (s) => s === "ready" }), Effect.timeout("10 seconds"), Effect.catchTag("TimeoutError", () => Effect.succeed("gave up" as const)))

exercises.title: Reading configuration
hints: Config.String takes the name of the key. A Config is an Effect, so yield* it.
const host = yield* Config.String("HOST")

exercises.title: Numbers, flags and ports
hints: Each constructor takes the key name. Values in a provider are text; the Config converts them.
const port = yield* Config.Port("PORT"); const debug = yield* Config.Boolean("DEBUG"); const retries = yield* Config.Int("RETRIES"); const rate = yield* Config.Number("RATE")

exercises.title: A default for a missing setting
hints: withDefault is applied with pipe, and takes the default value.
Config.Int("RETRIES").pipe(Config.withDefault(3))

exercises.title: An optional setting
hints: option wraps a Config and gives an Option: none when the key is missing.
Config.option(Config.String("PROXY"))

exercises.title: Several settings at once
hints: Config.all takes an object of Configs, like Effect.all.
Config.all({ host: Config.String("HOST"), port: Config.Port("PORT") })

exercises.title: Grouping settings under a prefix
hints: nested takes the Config and the name of the group.
Config.nested(Config.all({ url: Config.String("url"), pool: Config.Int("pool") }), "db")

exercises.title: The environment as a provider
hints: fromEnvRecord takes an object shaped like process.env. Nested names are joined with underscores.
ConfigProvider.layer(ConfigProvider.fromEnvRecord({ APP_PORT: "3000" }))

exercises.title: When the configuration is wrong
hints: A bad or missing setting fails with a ConfigError, whose tag is "ConfigError".
Config.Port("PORT").pipe(Effect.catchTag("ConfigError", () => Effect.succeed(3000)))

exercises.title: Secrets that do not leak
hints: Config.Redacted reads the setting as a Redacted value. Redacted.value is how you deliberately get the secret.
const apiKey = yield* Config.Redacted("API_KEY"); ...Redacted.value(apiKey)

exercises.title: Adjusting and falling back
hints: map transforms the value, orElse tries another Config when the first fails.
Config.Int("TIMEOUT_SECONDS").pipe(Config.map((s) => s * 1000)) and Config.String("NEW_NAME").pipe(Config.orElse(() => Config.String("OLD_NAME")))

exercises.title: Configuration described by a Schema
hints: Config.schema takes a Schema.Struct whose fields are the setting names.
Config.schema(Schema.Struct({ HOST: Schema.String, PORT: Schema.NumberFromString }))

exercises.title: Services that configure themselves
hints: Read the config inside the generator you give to Layer.effect, then build the service from it.
Layer.effect(Server, Effect.gen(function*() { const host = yield* Config.String("HOST"); const port = yield* Config.Port("PORT"); return Server.of({ address: `${host}:${port}` }) }))

exercises.title: Translate: process.env
hints: Each line of the plain version becomes one Config. Combine them with Config.all.
Config.all({ name: Config.String("APP_NAME"), workers: Config.Int("WORKERS").pipe(Config.withDefault(4)) })

exercises.title: Writing log lines
hints: Each one is a function that takes the message and returns an Effect. Yield it.
yield* Effect.logInfo("started"); yield* Effect.logWarning("slow"); yield* Effect.logError("failed"); yield* Effect.logDebug("details")

exercises.title: Effect.log and the default level
hints: Effect.log with no level is the same as Effect.logInfo.
The level is Info.

exercises.title: Attaching context to logs
hints: annotateLogs applies to every log inside the program it wraps.
work.pipe(Effect.annotateLogs({ requestId: "r-1", user: "ada" }))

exercises.title: Timing a section of logs
hints: withLogSpan takes a label. Every log inside carries it, with the elapsed time.
work.pipe(Effect.withLogSpan("checkout"))

exercises.title: Showing debug messages
hints: The minimum level is a service. Override it with Effect.provideService for just this program.
program.pipe(Effect.provideService(References.MinimumLogLevel, "Debug"))

exercises.title: Your own logger
hints: Logger.make takes a function from the log options to anything. Logger.layer takes an array of loggers.
Logger.make((options) => { lines.push(`${options.logLevel}: ${String(options.message)}`) }) and Logger.layer([logger])

exercises.title: Logging failures as they pass
hints: tapError runs an effect for the error without handling it. logError is such an effect.
call.pipe(Effect.tapError((e) => Effect.logError(`call failed: ${e}`)), Effect.catch(() => Effect.succeed("fallback")))

exercises.title: Counting things
hints: Define the counter once, at the top level. update adds to it. value reads its state.
const requests = Metric.counter("requests"); yield* Metric.update(requests, 1)

exercises.title: Measuring real work
hints: Count in tap for successes and tapError for failures.
Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(succeeded, 1)), Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(failed, 1))

exercises.title: Values that go up and down
hints: A gauge holds the latest value you set, like a speedometer. update replaces it.
yield* Metric.update(inFlight, 5); yield* Metric.update(inFlight, 3)

exercises.title: Distributions
hints: Update the histogram with each latency. The state has count, sum, min and max.
yield* Metric.update(latency, 12); ...; const state = yield* Metric.value(latency); return { count: state.count, sum: state.sum, min: state.min, max: state.max }

exercises.title: Counting categories
hints: A frequency counts how many times each text value was recorded.
yield* Metric.update(statuses, "ok"); then Object.fromEntries((yield* Metric.value(statuses)).occurrences)

exercises.title: Labelling metrics
hints: withAttributes returns a new metric that records under those labels.
Metric.withAttributes(requests, { route: "/users" })

exercises.title: Tracing: spans
hints: withSpan takes the name of the span and wraps a program.
Effect.sleep("1 millis").pipe(Effect.withSpan("load-user"))

exercises.title: Spans nest
hints: A span started while another is running becomes its child automatically.
Wrap the child steps in their own withSpan, and the whole generator in the parent's.

exercises.title: Details on a span
hints: annotateCurrentSpan is an Effect that adds a key and value to the span that is running now.
yield* Effect.annotateCurrentSpan("userId", id)

exercises.title: Effect.fn already traces
hints: Effect.fn("name") creates a span called "name" every time the function runs.
Just write the function with Effect.fn("loadOrder"); no withSpan is needed.

exercises.title: Capstone: an instrumented operation
hints: Use Effect.fn("placeOrder") for the span. Read the limit with a default of 3, annotate the span, then log, count and fail as the rules say.
Fail with TooMany when qty is above the limit, and count failures with tapError.
